Class SystemThemeDetector

java.lang.Object
ua.stetsenkoinna.theme.SystemThemeDetector
public final class SystemThemeDetector extends Object
Asks the desktop whether it is currently in dark mode.

Java has no portable API for this, so each desktop is asked in the only way it answers: the registry on Windows, the global defaults domain on macOS, and GSettings on the GNOME-derived Linux desktops. All three are separate processes, which is why the answer is cached - see detect() for when that cache is dropped.

Every path here is allowed to fail. A machine with no reg on PATH, a Linux desktop that is not GNOME, a locked-down sandbox that refuses to fork - all of them simply produce Optional.empty(), and the caller falls back to light, which is the appearance the app has always had. Being unable to detect the desktop's preference is not an error worth interrupting a startup for.

The command output parsers are package-private and pure, so they can be tested without a desktop of the relevant kind - which matters, since no single CI machine has all three.

  • Method Details

    • detect

      public static Optional<ThemeVariant> detect()
      Returns:
      the desktop's current appearance, or empty when this desktop cannot be asked

      Cached after the first call, because the answer costs a process and is wanted on the startup path. The cache is dropped by refresh(), which the theme is re-applied through - so a user who changes their desktop to dark and then reopens the theme menu sees the new answer, while a repaint never pays for one.

    • refresh
